lines.en: : Ami, where are you taking me?
: I told you the first ten times you asked! Somewhere you’re going to like! The answer hasn’t changed!
: I just can’t help but feel like you are lying to me considering every single building I can see from here sells nothing but anime and nerd stuff.
: Okay, first off, Sensei...anime isn’t just for nerds and I know you’re better than thinking that.
: Am I really, though?
: We used to watch Sailor Moon all the time when I was little!
: So obviously I would still love it years later.
: Exactly.
: That was sarcasm.
: Your face is sarcasm. Now stop asking where we’re going and let me lead the way!
Ami pulls me through the streets of the red-ish light entertainment district after a mildly long bus ride back from the cemetery.
Is this where I expected to come immediately succeeding one of the most emotional moments I have witnessed in the last...forever? No.
But I guess it will, to some extent, numb some of the pain she must be feeling right now.
Besides, indulging in her interests every now and again might not be the worst thing ever in exchange for a guaranteed life worth of smooth sailing and even smoother omelets.
I just hope we don’t have to spend the entire day here. I don’t like that a place as loud and bright as this is on the brink of becoming another regular location for me.
And I also don’t like that we are now walking into a nerd store.
: So, as you can see, I lied to you.
: Betrayed by my own [niece].
: Aren’t you the one who is supposed to always be on my side?
: I am on your side! I just knew that you wouldn’t come here with me if I told you the truth about where we were going, and the new volume of a manga I like came out today.
: There’s no [incest] in it at all.
: I mean, what? Who said that?
: Oh, look! New figures!
: Did you really have to come here today? Shouldn’t we have done something at least partially enjoyable for me?
: Oh, come on! We won’t be here long. I’m using my own money and everything.

: I just need to pick this up before all the new copies sell out and then we can go out and have our cute family date that I’m definitely not pretending is a real date and that we’re going to get married.
: I mean, what? Who keeps saying all of these weird things out of literally nowhere?
: Ami, I think you have a problem.
: It’s not me who’s wrong. It’s society.
: Now, come with me and don’t look at the back section of the store.
: Why can’t I look at the back section of the store?
: I will tell you when you’re older.
: Over here, Sensei!
: I’m more than twice your age. I think.
: How old are you again, Ami?
: Old enough! But that’s not a thing we should be yelling about in the store and you should probably come over here now!
I swallow the last few shreds of pride in my body (If that’s where pride is stored) and make my way over to Ami as she sifts through a bunch of brightly colored boxes and books.
And, despite apparently knowing exactly what she is here for, she sure takes her time in picking up and observing a lot of different items.
Have I been lied to again in such quick succession?
Is this the so-called “rebellious phase” I have heard of?
Is there a cut-off for when you can put someone up for adoption? Is that still a possibility if this keeps up?
: You know, Sensei, I can probably find something here for you if you want me to.
: And why would I want you to do that, exactly?
: Because...manga is more interesting than standing around and doing nothing all day?
: I don’t do “nothing” all day. You clearly don’t understand the first thing about how exciting my life is.
: If it’s so exciting how come you haven’t smiled in like six million years?
: I’m just waiting for the right moment.
: Uh-huh. Sure you are.
: Really, though! There’s tons of stuff here I think you would like! And I’m not just saying that because I think it would be nice to share a hobby with you.
: Niki told me about how you two used to watch anime together, so what if we got you something...retro? Like something you guys watched way back when?
: They even remake more popular series that have been out of style for a while sometimes. I’m sure I can find-
: I’m going to stop you right there at the risk of you making me feel even older than I constantly feel around you.
: If it makes you feel any better, I probably wouldn’t like you as much if you weren’t so much older and bigger than me.
: I mean, what? Really, where are all of these comments coming from?
: I’m gonna get you something. I’ve decided.
: And I’ve decided that you’re not going to do that.
: But it’s a present! I never got you anything for Christmas. Are you really going to turn away a free thing that your [niece] lovingly selected for you?
: Yes.
: What kind of genre do you want? Action? Drama? BL?
: What is BL?
: BL is-
: What’s this?! Time for another weebnote?!
: Oh. Molly’s here.
: That makes sense.
: BL, or “boys love” is a wildly underappreciated genre in the anime and manga world where, get this- boys love each other!
: Why would you even suggest that for me?
: Because I think it’d be hot.
: What?
: Did you know that BL manga dates all the way back to the mid-70’s? It hasn’t changed much since then and is still aimed primarily at young girls, but the origins were actually much darker!
: Kaze to Ki no Uta, which is commonly referred to as the first instance of the BL genre, features stuff like prostitution, drug usage, and ra-
: Uhh...actually, that’s it for today’s weebnote. I don’t really have anything else to say.
: What brings you here, Molly? I thought you and Tsuneyo were supposed to hang out today.
: I am Tsuneyo.
: Surprise. I am also here.
: I’m assuming you were dragged along unwillingly as well?
: Not at all, Sir. It was actually Tsuneyo’s idea to come here, not mine. I spent everything I currently have on gacha games, so I’m only here to act as a consult today.
: Tsuneyo’s finally getting into manga?
: I received a Christmas bonus from my father and feel the need to spend it on things I am supposed to appreciate before it is too late and he asks for it back.
: I don’t think employers ever ask for bonuses back, but I guess I don’t know your dad all that well.
: He does not like summer very much. I will not squander this opportunity to buy a brightly colored rectangle.
: How about you, Ami? What are you doing here?
: The new volume of My Sweet Prince came out today and I wanted to make sure I got it before it was sold out.
: My Sweet Prince? Isn’t that the one where the girl and her uncle-
: Oh my god.
: Hmm hm hmmmm~
In a strange twist of fate, it looks like Ami lied again and that the book she’s buying very much has the one thing she told me it didn’t have.
: Well I guess that confirms that suspicion.
: Just liking a certain trope in manga doesn’t mean you like it in real life, Molly. Everybody knows that.
: It normally does, though.
: I won’t confirm nor deny anything.
: I take it that means you two are...on a...date then?
: No.
: Mm!
: Wait. Now I’m confused. Is this not a meeting of secret, forbidden love? A taste testing of the most bitter fruit of all?
: I believe that would be the “bitter melon,” which is famous for its medicinal properties.
: We’re just stopping by on our way back from...a place.
: That...
: You know that makes it sound even sketchier...don’t you, Sir?
: I don’t know where your depraved mind goes after just hearing the word “place,” but I can assure you it’s not whatever you’re thinking.
: I doubt Ami wants to talk about it, though, so let’s just move on and-
: I wanted to see my mom.
: I’ve just missed her a lot lately. That’s all.
: Which is why we’re now...counteracting that with some place happy and...
: May I hug you?
: Yes, please.
Molly wraps her arms around Ami and pulls her close, pressing their heads together.
They gaze into each other’s eyes and, if this weren’t such a heartfelt moment, I’d probably say something to emphasize just how much I’d appreciate it if the two of them would kiss right now.
Which is obviously not a thing I’m going to talk about.
I mean, how could anyone think that at a time like this?
Nope. I don’t want that to happen at all.
Not even a little.
Not even a little.
: I lost my mom when I was little, too. I know what it’s like.
: I know...I always wanted to ask you about how you managed to...talk about it so easily, but...it’s hard, you know?
: I do. But you know what’s easier? Hugging. So I hereby give you permission to hug me any time you want as a free action.
: Thank you, Molly. I’ll be here for you if you ever need me, too.
: I’ll remember that.
: Hey, how come we never do anything with just the two of us?
: Probably because you already have Ayane and Maya and I would just be getting in the way.
: Let’s hang out soon. Just us.
: I’d like that a lot...
Not even a little.
: It appears everyone has forgotten that I lack a mother as well.
: Ah! I’m sorry, Kendo Princess! I just know that...your affinity for hugs is not as high as mine! And that you wouldn’t want to get involved in something like this...
: And I just...wasn’t even thinking. Sorry, Tsuneyo.
: Abandoned by my own party members. I truly am an outcast.
: I’ll hug you, Tsuneyo. We don’t need them.
: I would rather die.
: That...seems like an exaggeration.
: It is not.
: Didn’t we hug on Halloween that one time?
: I have no idea what you are talking about.
: When-
: I would never hug a man as horrible as you.
: It was after we went outside and-
: Never.
: And Molly was-
: It would simply not happen.
: But-
: Just give it a rest, Sir. Your charisma isn’t high enough to break through to Tsuneyo yet.
: That’s fine, but...
: How long are you two going to stay like that for?
: Maybe just a little bit longer.
: Ahh, youth...
: Tsuneyo, you’re the same age as them.
: Then why will no one hug me?
: I literally just offered-
: No thank you.
: You smell really nice.
: I was actually just about to say the same thing to you.

I guess Ami winds up mistaking Molly for a relative or something since it seems she has a hard time separating from her, but I’m sure it’s probably closer to the fact that she just has someone she can relate to.
Even if Ayane’s mom isn’t around anymore, I can’t imagine Ami being able to confide in her in the way that she could with someone who’s actually felt the same sort of pain she has.
But pain is not something I intend to dwell on any longer when its abundance is one of many things in this life that neither myself nor anyone else is able to avoid.
I will focus on the brighter things and what it is that illuminates them.
Ami finds her manga (Which may or may not contain [incest], but probably does) and pays for it at the register after separating from the others.
She clutches it to her chest as the two of us exit the store together and make our way out into the street, bustling with foot traffic due to the sudden increase in temperature.
Then, before long, she’s pulling me around once again.
Just...
Hopefully to somewhere I won’t feel out of place in this time.
Ami’s affection has increased to [ami_love]!
